inheritanceRule: Every omitted field inherits the resolved unchained Summoner parent value.

profiles.name: Construct Caller

evidence.reason: The eidolon is locked to the inevitable subtype and all summon-monster uses are exchanged for additional evolution points.

profiles.playerSummary: A planar tinkerer who gives up temporary summons to build a more heavily evolved construct-like inevitable eidolon.
profiles.tradeoff: The eidolon gains five additional evolution points, but its subtype is fixed and the entire summon-monster spell-like progression is lost.

profiles.name: Devil Binder

constraints.summary: A Devil Binder must be lawful evil or lawful neutral.
The eidolon must have the devil subtype and accepts major martial limitations.

evidence.reason: The eidolon gains a full ladder of offensive spell-like abilities while the summoner gains infernal bloodline attacks.
Suggestion, charm monster, dominate person and power word stun make magical disabling central.
The summoner develops wings and progressively assumes infernal physical traits.

profiles.playerSummary: A lawful binder who weakens a devil eidolon’s martial chassis in exchange for powerful infernal magic shared between master and servant.
profiles.tradeoff: Alignment and eidolon subtype are locked, the eidolon loses attack progression, and normal summoning is replaced by limited spell-like abilities.

profiles.name: Devil Impostor

evidence.reason: Bluff and Intimidate become class skills and the eidolon can use its master’s social training.
False alignment auras and a convincing devil disguise support sustained deception.
The summoner can dismiss the eidolon and assume its apparent devil form for hours.

profiles.playerSummary: A deceiver who disguises any eidolon as a devil, falsifies infernal auras and can personally assume the eidolon’s form.
profiles.tradeoff: Several protective bond features are exchanged for disguise and social deception, while summoned monsters are forced into the fiendish template.

profiles.name: Fey Caller

evidence.reason: Broad social skills and charm, suggestion, illusion and disguise magic define the fey bond.
Summon nature’s ally, Knowledge (nature), Survival and woodland stride replace planar generalism.

profiles.playerSummary: A nature-oriented summoner who calls creatures from the summon nature’s ally list and bonds with a magically gifted fey eidolon.
profiles.tradeoff: The eidolon subtype and temporary summon list become strongly fey-and-nature focused, reducing planar breadth.

profiles.name: God Caller

evidence.reason: The eidolon supplies guidance at will while close to the God Caller.
The eidolon amplifies Diplomacy and Intimidate and eventually commands groups supernaturally.

profiles.playerSummary: A community leader whose semi-divine eidolon advises allies, strengthens social influence and eventually projects an overwhelming presence.
profiles.tradeoff: The eidolon must remain unusually close to retain full hit points, and several personal/eidolon-sharing features are lost.

profiles.name: Leshy Caller

evidence.reason: The eidolon changes plant form by environment and temporary summoning uses nature’s ally with added leshys.

profiles.playerSummary: A First World summoner bonded to a plant-like leshy eidolon whose body and movement can adapt to the surrounding environment.
profiles.tradeoff: The eidolon and summon list become nature-specific rather than offering the parent’s broad outsider themes.

profiles.name: Soulbound Summoner

constraints.summary: The Summoner must select a permanent oracle curse reflecting the accidental soul bond.

evidence.reason: All summon-monster and gate spell-like abilities are lost to concentrate additional power and spell access in one eidolon.

profiles.playerSummary: An accidental summoner whose eidolon lives within the psyche, bears the same alignment and grows far more adaptable through an intense soul bond.
profiles.tradeoff: A permanent oracle curse applies and all temporary summoning is lost, concentrating almost the entire class identity in one eidolon.

profiles.name: Storm Caller

constraints.summary: The eidolon subtype must provide electricity resistance or immunity.

evidence.reason: Scaling lightning bolts and a line of electricity between summoner and eidolon become signature attacks.
Call-lightning bolts and the summoner-eidolon lightning line attack areas or multiple creatures.
The Summoner progressively gains a permanent flight evolution.

profiles.playerSummary: An air-and-electricity specialist who summons storm creatures, calls repeated lightning and eventually flies alongside the eidolon.
profiles.tradeoff: The eidolon and summon list are tightly restricted by electricity themes, and several bond and teleportation features are replaced.

profiles.name: Twinned Summoner
profiles.sourceCitationText: Legacy of the First World pg. 18

evidence.reason: Every teamwork feat gained by the Summoner is automatically granted to the eidolon.
Master and eidolon can swap positions at range, eventually as a swift action.

profiles.playerSummary: A Summoner whose humanoid eidolon appears as a twin, automatically shares teamwork feats and rapidly swaps places in battle.
profiles.tradeoff: The eidolon’s form is restricted and several protective and merging abilities are exchanged for coordination and position-swapping.
